message:
Hi. I'm off to Lisbon next week for a three-day work trip, my first time in Portugal, and I want to travel carry-on only this time, after the airline lost my case in the spring.

Could you suggest three things to do in Lisbon on a free evening? And how do I say "thank you" in Portuguese? Is it different depending on who's saying it? And is tipping expected in restaurants there, or is that more of an American thing?

My wheeled bag measures 56 × 36 × 23 cm including the wheels and handle, and packed it weighs 9 kg. Will it meet the carry-on limit?

Also, recommend a packing approach: rolling or folding for work shirts? I need a short out-of-office message that's professional but not stiff, since most of my contacts are clients rather than colleagues. And what's a good colour for a luggage tag so it's easy to spot? I'm flying back on the Friday evening, straight after a full day of meetings, so anything that makes the return journey less stressful is welcome.

Thanks a lot.
response:
Here's everything in order. The bag question depends on your airline, so I've started there.

## Will your bag fit as carry-on?

It depends on the airline, and your bag is right on the edge of several common limits:

| Airline (economy) | Size limit | Weight limit | Your bag (56 × 36 × 23 cm, 9 kg) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TAP Air Portugal | 55 × 40 × 20 cm | 8 kg | Too deep and too heavy |
| Ryanair (Priority) | 55 × 40 × 20 cm | 10 kg | Too deep |
| easyJet (large cabin bag) | 56 × 45 × 25 cm | 15 kg | Fits |
| British Airways | 56 × 45 × 25 cm | 23 kg | Fits |

The depth is the main problem: 23 cm against a 20 cm limit on many airlines. Allowances also vary by fare type and change from time to time, so check your booking. If you tell me the airline and fare, I can be more specific.

If the bag is borderline, it's more likely to be checked at the gate. Since avoiding checked bags is your whole goal, a 20 cm-deep bag may be worth it if you fly these airlines often.

## Three things for a free evening

1. **Sunset at a viewpoint (*miradouro*).** Senhora do Monte has the widest view; Santa Luzia and São Pedro de Alcântara are more central.
2. **Fado.** This is Portugal's traditional melancholy song. Alfama and Mouraria have small restaurants with live fado over dinner, and Bairro Alto has more casual bars. Booking ahead helps.
3. **The riverfront and Baixa.** Walk down to Praça do Comércio as the lights come on, then have a pastel de nata or dinner nearby. Time Out Market (Mercado da Ribeira) is easy if you're short on time.

## Saying "thank you"

- **Obrigado** if you're a man, **obrigada** if you're a woman.
- It depends on the speaker's gender, not the listener's.
- **Muito obrigado/a** means "thank you very much."

## Tipping

Tipping isn't expected the way it is in the US. Service isn't usually added to the bill. In sit-down restaurants, people often round up or leave around 5–10% for good service, but nobody will mind if you don't.

One useful thing to know: bread, olives or cheese placed on the table at the start (the *couvert*) are charged if you eat them. Send them back if you don't want them.

## Packing work shirts

**Fold work shirts and roll everything else.** Rolling tends to crease collars and leave lines across shirt fronts. A neat approach:
- Button the shirts, fold them flat, and stack them, alternating collar direction.
- Put rolled soft items (underwear, T-shirts) around the edges to keep the stack from shifting.

Hang the shirts in the bathroom while you shower when you arrive, and most creases will drop out. Most business hotels also have an iron.

## Out-of-office message

> Thank you for your email. I'm travelling for work from [date] to [date] and will have limited access to email during this time. I'll reply as soon as I can after I'm back on [return date].
>
> If your message is urgent, please contact [name] at [email/phone], who will be glad to help.
>
> Best regards,
> [Your name]

## Luggage tag colour

Pick something bright and uncommon: **fluorescent orange, lime green or hot pink**. Red and black are everywhere. A bright strap or ribbon on the handle helps too. Even with carry-on, it's worth having in case your bag gets gate-checked.

## Making Friday's return easier

- **Pack completely on Thursday night.** Leave out only Friday's clothes and a toiletries bag.
- **Check out on Friday morning.** Either take the bag to your meetings or leave it at the hotel and collect it on the way, depending on your route to the airport.
- **Check in online and keep your boarding pass on your phone.** Liquids should already be in their clear bag.
- **Allow plenty of time.** Lisbon airport is close to the centre, about 20–30 minutes by taxi or Uber, or you can take the metro's red line. But Friday traffic and airport queues can both be slow, so aim to arrive about two hours before your flight.
- **Eat before security** if your meetings run through dinner, so you're not relying on what's open airside.
- **Keep your passport, phone and charger in one dedicated pocket** so you're not searching for them.

Have a good trip.
